title: PRD: Milestone 10 — Epic 2: Dependency Security and License Compliance
summary: Requirements for supply-chain hardening: config-driven cargo audit, OSV-Scanner, Snyk evaluation, cargo-deny license policy, and CycloneDX SBOM on releases.
notes: MANIFEST_TYPE=PRD supplied and content confirms (user stories, goals, FR list, non-goals, success metrics). Stated policy captured verbatim in scope: FR1 requires cargo audit ignore-list sourced from version-controlled audit.toml (single source of truth) instead of inline --ignore flags so workflow and config cannot drift; FR3 requires each audit.toml exception to carry advisory ID, affected crate/why present, why unfixable, revisit condition; existing RUSTSEC-2023-0071 and RUSTSEC-2025-0111 exceptions must be preserved. License posture (FR11): allow MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, ISC, Zlib; GPL-*/AGPL-*/LGPL-* not allowed absent explicit recorded justification; FR14 forbids blanket disabling of the license check, requiring either allow-list addition with justification or a narrowly-scoped per-crate clarify/exception. FR12 sets bans with no banned crates initially and duplicate versions surfaced at least as warn (Open Question 4: multiple-versions starts at warn, not deny). Success metric: audit.toml and deny.toml are the only places policy/exceptions are defined; no inline advisory-ignore flags remain in CI. Document is silent on the `license = "MIT"` vs `MIT OR Apache-2.0` manifest discrepancy noted by the orchestrator — not recorded here, no inference made.
